review_evidence: README states and documents the headline Church–Rosser/confluence theorem for the eleven φ-calculus normalization rules, proved via parallel reduction and the Takahashi diamond.
The PhiConfluence tree formalizes syntax, well-formedness, one-step and parallel reduction, preservation, diamond/confluence, convertibility, and an executable reducer with reduce_sound.
A declaration scan finds 92 theorem/lemma/example/axiom declarations; the source is an independently addressable formal semantics/proof development.
summary: Retain objectionary/proof, a machine-checked confluence development for φ-calculus normalization.

review_evidence: .github/axioms.lean is a real Lean file: it imports PhiConfluence and runs #print axioms on PhiConfluence.confluence, conv_equivalence, reduce_sound, par_triangle, parWF_diamond, nf_iff, and contextualize_eq_self; it names the main results and is not CI configuration.

Main.lean defines `examples : List (String × Term)`, concrete phi-calculus terms that exercise each normalization rule (Rdd, Rnull, Rmiss, Rover, Rstay, Rskip, Ralpha, Rcopy, Rdot, Rdl), plus an IO demo that traces the certified reducer.
Difftest.lean defines `cases : List Term` (30 annotated phi-terms with their expected normal forms) and `normalForm`; these are formal Term definitions, not a shell script.

PhiConfluence/Render.lean declares `structure RuleSpec` and the definitions ppRule, ppAttr, ppByte, ppBytes, and the mutual ppTerm/ppBindings/ppBinding by pattern matching over the Term, Attr, and Binding inductive types.
PhiConfluence.lean holds only import lines; FILTER-007 keeps it primary-eligible because no auxiliary delivery path is verified.

The other PhiConfluence/* modules carry declarations: Parallel.lean has 64 theorem/def/inductive lines, Preservation.lean 14, Reduce.lean 10, and Attributes, WellFormed, Normal, Confluence, Diamond, Nf, LocalConfluence, RuleSchema, Syntax, Step, Context, and Abstract/Rewriting each have at least one.
summary: Read the five candidate files in full (.github/axioms.lean, Main.lean, Difftest.lean, PhiConfluence/Render.lean, PhiConfluence.lean) and counted declarations in the PhiConfluence/* modules. Every file is Lean source of the phi-calculus confluence development: definitions, theorems, or Lean commands that reference its named results. No file meets the FILTER-002/FILTER-004 bar, so the whole unit is retained.
